Available in the public release

Two files. One live tile.

A native JavaScript tile is a small local package: a manifest and a render(ctx) function. Return display data; ReStart draws the tile. Start with a bundled example, or try this minimal clock.

manifest.json · native format, version 1
{
  "version": 1,
  "title": "My clock",
  "refreshSeconds": 1,
  "settings": {}
}
tile.js
function render(ctx) {
  const now = new Date(ctx.now);
  return {
    text: now.toLocaleTimeString(ctx.locale),
    detail: ctx.calendar.weekday,
    background: "#123448",
    foreground: "#FFFFFF"
  };
}

Put both files in one folder. Import manifest.json from ReStart’s JavaScript tile settings. ReStart installs its own copy, so later edits belong in the installed package. For repeat use, place package folders in the local tile library.

Useful input, without the plumbing

A snapshot of the moment.

The host provides JSON context for each update. Respond to the current tile size, local PC time, a click, or a new data snapshot. Use the previous successful state for a local counter, chart history or timer.

ContextWhat it gives you
ctx.sizeSmall, medium, wide or large. Choose a layout that fits.
ctx.timePC wall-clock time, UTC offset and monotonic uptime.
ctx.languageThe selected UI language; ctx.locale helps format values.
ctx.eventA local click event, when one is pending.
ctx.stateYour last successful JSON state for this session.
ctx.systemAggregate CPU, memory, network, battery and storage metrics when requested.
ctx.dataCached values from explicitly configured JSON or RSS/Atom inputs.

The public version 1 renderer is synchronous and returns bounded native display data. It does not expose a DOM, Node.js, general filesystem access or direct networking.

Bring in something useful

Your data. A small window into it.

Declare a named input in the manifest. The user chooses and enables its connection locally. The host handles fetching, caching and retry backoff; your tile reads the latest snapshot.

Manifest capability and named data input
{
  "version": 1,
  "title": "Service status",
  "capabilities": ["data.sources"],
  "dataSources": {
    "service": { "format": "json", "refreshSeconds": 60 }
  }
}

Keep connections local. URLs, selected files and optional credential headers belong in ReStart’s connection settings, not in a shared tile package. Selected response data reaches the script; connection credentials do not.

In development · Not in the public download yet

A canvas for your HTML & CSS.

The next tile format is being developed around HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript, within ReStart’s four fixed tile sizes. It will bring SVG, Canvas, transparent backgrounds and custom typography to the tile surface, alongside a built-in authoring workspace.

Existing native packages remain supported. The API and authoring workflow are still being verified; use the public format above for a tile you want to share with current-release users.

Run the source

A Windows app, in the open.

ReStart uses C#, WPF and the stable .NET SDK selected by global.json. Build on Windows. The repository keeps the app, core models and isolated JavaScript worker in separate projects.

PowerShell · from the repository root
dotnet restore ReStart.slnx --locked-mode
dotnet build ReStart.slnx -c Release --no-restore
dotnet test ReStart.slnx -c Release --no-build

The commands above build and test a developer checkout. Portable distribution packages have their own script, runtime bundles and notice files.
